create.name: His Holiness the Dalai Lama
create.bio:
Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, calls himself a simple Buddhist monk. He was born Lhamo Dhondup in 1935 into a farming family in Amdo, in north-eastern Tibet, and was recognised at the age of two as the rebirth of the 13th Dalai Lama. His monastic training began when he was six and followed the Nalanda curriculum, centred on Buddhist philosophy, and in 1959 he passed his final examination in Lhasa and received the Geshe Lharampa degree. Since going into exile that same year he has lived in Dharamsala, in northern India.

His teaching rests on three commitments he describes on his own site. As a human being, he encourages people to be happy by training the mind and growing warm-heartedness, compassion, forgiveness, patience and contentment, values he calls secular ethics because they can help anyone, whether or not they follow a religion. As a monk, he works for harmony and respect between the world's faiths. As a Tibetan, he cares for the language and culture that came down from the masters of Nalanda. He also takes a keen interest in what ancient Indian understanding of the mind and practices such as meditation can offer modern education. His talks and teachings are free of charge, and his office shares many of them as videos online.
